candidate_relations.label: Radiation Proctitis, chronic
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a single deep-cratered ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with the remainder of the rectum appearing normal (no diffuse radiation-induced changes), which is characteristic of a solitary rectal ulcer rather than radiation proctitis. Radiation proctitis typically involves diffuse mucosal changes, friability, and telangiectasias throughout the irradiated segment. While both are radiation-related rectal conditions, solitary rectal ulcer and radiation proctitis are distinct diagnoses with different endoscopic, histologic, and management profiles. Asserting chronic radiation proctitis conflicts with the focal, solitary ulcer morphology and the explicitly normal surrounding rectal mucosa documented here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Radiation proctitis is a broader/different entity encompassing diffuse mucosal inflammation; the reference specifies a solitary rectal ulcer as the discrete focal lesion type, which is a distinct clinical and pathological entity from radiation proctitis

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis specifies 'radiation-induced solitary rectal ulcer' — a focal entity distinct from radiation proctitis; the normal surrounding rectal mucosa on colonoscopy is a key discriminating feature
